title: Flat Tag Identity Concept
summary: separate globally unique tag identity from one scalar analytical group while leaving contextual nuance to linked document content
content_html:
Flat Tag Identity Concept

Purpose

Keep the identity used by work and series assignments independent from tag classification. Subject, domain, form, and theme remain allowed analytical groups, but they are not identity namespaces.

Mental model

moss is the tag and subject is its one group. A document may explain moss as depicted material, ecological domain, metaphor, theme, or any other useful context. Those readings are prose, not separate canonical tags or additional group memberships.

flat tag identity
  -> classified by one registry group
  -> assigned to work and series records
  -> linked one way to one explanatory document
  -> interpreted through document content

Invariants

  • tag_id is the globally unique normalized tag name.
  • Every registry tag has exactly one required scalar group from the allowed group policy. A groups array is not supported.
  • Tag identity has no group prefix, and no consumer infers group from tag_id.
  • Filtering, scoring, coverage, styling, alias constraints, and report metadata resolve group through the registry record.
  • Contextual differences between previously namespaced instances are resolved in one document rather than represented as parallel registry rows.
  • Assignment data records the tag only; it does not record which interpretation motivated an assignment or duplicate the registry group.
  • The registry remains the assignment identity authority.
  • Changing a tag's group does not change tag_id or rewrite assignments, but it is a validated registry mutation because it can affect aliases, reports, and scoring.
  • After Tag-document linking, the associated document is the semantic authority; registry prose is removed rather than synchronized.
  • The registry holds the one-way tag_id to doc_id relationship. Documents do not carry a tag_id back-reference, and unrelated documents may remain unreferenced.

Collision decision

Labels repeated across namespaces are not mechanically collapsed. Each collision is reviewed to choose one flat identity, exactly one group, its assignments and aliases, and document content that can carry the useful contextual distinctions.

The migration may preserve several genuinely different tags only by giving them genuinely different names, with one group for each resulting tag. It must not recreate namespaced identity through compatibility prefixes or aliases.

The separate schema decision to remove the registry label duplicated by flat tag_id is complete and is owned by Tag Registry Label Retirement Delivery.
